texts: mixed: the sky-cat, the hunting and summer all come through, but "through summer" flattens to a bare summer time-stamp, so the fact reads as a hunt at some point in summer rather than one lasting the whole season. Rewrite as "A sky-cat hunts throughout the summer.": our translator has a proper whole-extent relation for "throughout" (and "during" / "while") but none for "through", so that one word swap keeps the season-long force without changing what you are saying.

mixed: the place is built correctly — the base bound as part of the cliff — and the open "what happens" is asked in the supported way, but "by autumn" reaches nothing: the translator can rank months and weekdays against each other and nothing ranks seasons, so the deadline collapses to "stamped autumn" and will miss the hunting your first sentence stamped summer. Give the deadline a month, and date the statements in months too: "What happens at the base of the cliff by September?"
